Rev. and the Solar Phys. reprint) have the identical three authors, so the selection cannot change who is taken. Semantic Scholar was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on every attempt; OpenAlex was used as the second literature index in its place.

Author-order detection, instrument papers (backward scan on normalized family names): CDS n=39 suffix 1; CELIAS n=33 suffix 1; COSTEP n=19 suffix 1; EIT n=28 suffix 3; ERNE n=15 suffix 6 from position 10 (partially alphabetized, prefix = positions 1-9); GOLF n=31 suffix 1; LASCO n=15 suffix 2; MDI n=12 suffix 6 from position 7 (partially alphabetized, prefix = positions 1-6); SUMER n=16 suffix 2; SWAN n=25 suffix 1; UVCS n=40 suffix 2; VIRGO n=25 suffix 4. Instrument-paper selection CONFIDENT for all twelve: each is the dedicated description paper in the Solar Physics 162 (1995) SOHO special issue, published the month of launch, with a large team author list, the instrument named in the title, and high citation counts (LASCO 2824, MDI 2413, EIT 1787, SUMER 797, CDS 573, UVCS 437, VIRGO 309, CELIAS 295, GOLF 237, ERNE 225, COSTEP 222 per OpenAlex). Three of the DOIs (CELIAS, COSTEP, ERNE) are cited by the SPASE Instrument records themselves, which anchors the whole contiguous DOI series.

Observatory scoping rule applied strictly and symmetrically: from each instrument paper only positions 1-3 (or prefix positions 1-3) were taken, at Strong. Every author at position 4 or beyond on all twelve instrument papers was excluded as instrument-team depth belonging to that Instrument record's own finder run - 262 people in total (298 authors across the twelve papers, minus the 36 taken), not enumerated individually. Where such a citation names an individual not already captured, that individual was included at Medium as a named lead of a record-cited description paper: Hoeksema (MDI), Lemaire (SUMER), Noci (UVCS). The full author lists of those proceedings papers could not be retrieved (they are cited as 'et al.'), so only the explicitly named individuals were taken, and at Medium rather than Strong.
